name: Hedonex
description: Hedonex is a synthetic neuropeptide cascade engineered to interface directly with BCI reward-pathway modules, flooding the nucleus accumbens and its synthetic analogs with a precisely calibrated dopamine-serotonin-endorphin cocktail. Unlike crude chemical euphoriants, it handshakes with the user's neural interface to amplify and sustain the signal far beyond natural limits. The result is a clean, overwhelming bliss with no chemical hangover — only the crushing weight of comparison to everything that came before.
effects: Sense of profound meaning and purpose
BCI-mediated pleasure wave cycling every 4-7 minutes
Feeling of being fundamentally loved and complete
side_effects: BCI feedback loops causing involuntary pleasure spikes days later
Reality dissatisfaction syndrome with extended use
Rare: neural interface desensitization requiring hardware recalibration
cultural_context: Hedonex was originally developed as post-surgical comfort medication for major augmentation procedures. It leaked into recreational markets within six months of approval. In Tier 3 and 4, it's the drug of ambitious people who work brutal hours — the reward they promise themselves. On the Shelf, bootleg versions cut with cheaper compounds circulate under the name God-Switch, and the anhedonia crash has been linked to a significant portion of Tier 1 suicide statistics.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 corporate analyst is burning through Hedonex doses to reward herself after each successful project — her tolerance is climbing and she's begun falsifying project outcomes just to justify the next hit

A Shelf street doc has synthesized a crude analog of Hedonex that skips the BCI handshake entirely, flooding reward centers chemically — it's cheaper, it works, and it's killing people in ways that look like cardiac events
Someone has figured out how to weaponize Hedonex by aerosolizing it in a confined space — the victims don't run, don't fight, don't want to do anything at all
